security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD kernel or bhyve hypervisor compiled against the pre-correction Smnip CSR address definitions uses the stale CSR number constants: msp at 0x348 (now mipreemptcfg), mipreemptcfg at 0x347 (now mithreshold), mithreshold at 0xFB1 (now unmapped), or sithreshold at 0x1B1 (now unmapped). A CSR read-modify-write on the old msp address 0x348 writes a stack pointer value into mipreemptcfg; conversely, a read of old mithreshold at 0xFB1 targets custom CSR space and returns garbage, corrupting interrupt enable logic. In FreeBSD's bhyve, guest CSR emulation using the old addresses passes incorrect register semantics to the VMM, allowing a guest to configure M-mode interrupt preemption by writing to what it believes is its stack pointer.
security_spec.summary: Stale Smnip CSR address constants cause cross-register aliasing: msp↔mipreemptcfg at 0x348 and mithreshold↔mipreemptcfg at 0x347 create a write-what-where primitive where stack pointer values land in interrupt preemption/threshold config, potentially escalating to M-mode interrupt hijack in bhyve guests

findings.finding: CSR address space between CSR_MIP (0x344) and CSR_PMPCFG0 (0x3a0) is clean. No stale Smnip/CLIC CSR constants (0x347, 0x348) are defined anywhere in the RISC-V headers. The CSR address table jumps from M-mode core CSRs directly to PMP registers with no intervening Smnip definitions.
CSR accessor macros (csr_swap/csr_write/csr_read/csr_set/csr_clear) use symbolic CSR names exclusively, never raw numeric addresses. No path exists to accidentally reference stale CSR addresses.

bhyve VMM guest CSR save/restore uses standard H-extension virtualized CSRs (vsstatus, vsie, vstvec, vsscratch, vsepc, vscause, vstval, hvip, vsatp). No Smnip/CLIC CSRs are saved or restored because FreeBSD does not implement CLIC interrupt handling at all.

Interrupt controller uses standard PLIC-based interrupt model with sie/sip CSR bits (SIE_SSIE, SIE_STIE, SIE_SEIE). No CLIC/Smnip threshold or preemption registers are referenced. Interrupt enable/disable logic operates on standard RISC-V privilege spec CSRs only.

The only CLIC reference in the entire sys/riscv tree is a comment about getting the hart ID from CLIC's phandle (device tree parsing). This is a device tree topology reference, not a CSR-level emulation or register definition. No CLIC CSR addresses are used.
findings.snippet: /* Get the hart ID from the CLIC's phandle. */

findings.finding: Trap handler validates sstatus fields (SPP, SIE, SUM) using standard RISC-V privileged architecture bit definitions from riscvreg.h. No Smnip-specific register access or validation is performed.

Complete CSR enumeration audit: no CSR constants exist at addresses 0x148 (ssp), 0x347 (old mipreemptcfg), 0x348 (old msp, now mipreemptcfg), 0xFB1 (old mithreshold), or 0x1B1 (old sithreshold). The encoding.h CSR table covers only ratified RISC-V privileged spec CSRs. The Smnip (CLIC) extension is entirely absent from FreeBSD's CSR infrastructure.
findings.snippet:
CSR table: 0x100-0x180 (S-mode), 0x300-0x344 (M-mode), 0x3a0-0x3bf (PMP),
  0x7a0-0x7b2 (debug), 0xb00-0xb9f (M-mode counters), 0xc00-0xc9f (S-mode counters),
  0xf11-0xf14 (M-mode info). No 0x147-0x348 or 0xFB1 range entries.
